items.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001
items.q: Well I was working with Art Blakey so— ... And at the end of the set he looked up and saw me and I was hired.

ctx.x: Yeah. There was a lot. But there was a little bit left by the time I was fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, and I got out to hear that. I heard Art Blakey, I heard Johnny Griffin, and of course I heard Coltrane and I heard a lot of things, McCoy Tyner. It wasn’t like New York. And I always had a feeling that I wanted to be in New York, since I was six years © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

old I was drawing — and I’ve never heard or seen anything — but I was drawing these apartment buildings with little mice sticking out of them for people, like a lot of people in every window. It was very funny.
